title: Diurna
description: The world, every day, in three sentences.

items.title: In Dublin, Volodymyr Zelensky announces a record prisoner swap and Europe’s seat at the table
items.content_html:
Ukraine’s president says Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, whom he received on Thursday evening on their way back from the Kremlin, promised him the biggest prisoner exchange of the war. Europeans are expected to join the next round of talks, though Moscow has not confirmed it.

On the evening of Thursday 12 November, at Baldonnel air base west of Dublin, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky, received America’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, a few hours after their meeting with Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin, the Kyiv Independent reports. Mr Zelensky says the meeting “unblocked” the three-way talks, paved the way for the largest exchange of prisoners of war since 2022 and secured direct European representation at the next session, with Mr Kushner arguing that no deal is possible without Europe, according to the Kyiv Post. No date has yet been set for the new round, whose format the Kremlin has not confirmed, while the “coalition of the willing” is due to meet in Berlin next week and EU leaders will weigh Kyiv’s financing needs for 2027 on 26-27 November.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Iran says it hit an American radar in Bahrain as Donald Trump rules out a deal
items.content_html:
The Revolutionary Guards claim to have destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain on Friday in retaliation for a strike on the port of Sirik, a claim America’s military disputes. A day earlier America’s president called a deal with Tehran unnecessary and took his vice-president off the file.

On Thursday 12 November Donald Trump wrote that America did “not need a deal with Iran” and told his vice-president, JD Vance, who had been considering a meeting with the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, to focus on crime in Democratic-run cities, Middle East Eye reports. The reversal, days after he spoke of “momentum” towards a settlement, comes as Tehran denies any planned meeting in Qatar, refuses to send its enriched uranium abroad and keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed until its conditions are met. On Friday 13 November the Revolutionary Guards said they had destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for an unclaimed strike on a telecoms tower in Sirik, on the Strait of Hormuz, while America’s Central Command says it shot down two drones, causing no damage, according to RFE/RL and Fox News.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Dogged by suspicions of Chinese espionage, Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia’s boss
items.content_html:
The co-founder of the AI-chip giant resigned on Thursday, after revelations of an affair with a woman whom American officials suspect of spying for Beijing. The chief financial officer, Colette Kress, takes over in the interim.

On Thursday 12 November Nvidia announced the resignation “effective immediately” of its chief executive and co-founder, Jensen Huang, 63, who also leaves the board, gave no official reason and named its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim boss, Al Jazeera and The National report. On 8 November he had admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm, whom American officials suspect of spying for Beijing, while Nvidia, which controls about 90% of the market for advanced AI chips, sits at the heart of the Sino-American technology rivalry. The shares fell by more than 14% at one point on Thursday, the board, now chaired by Harvey Jones, is looking for a successor, and Republican lawmakers are threatening a subpoena to question Mr Huang about the affair’s implications for national security.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.
tags: Nvidia and the China spying claims

items.title: Spain’s first general strike since 2012 puts housing at the heart of the election
items.content_html:
Hundreds of thousands marched through Spain’s big cities on Wednesday, answering the main unions’ call to protest against soaring rents and for higher wages. The mobilisation comes less than three weeks before the snap general election of 29 November.

On Wednesday 11 November Spain held its first general strike since 2012, called by the CCOO and UGT unions under the banner “wages, housing and prices”, which drew at least 120,000 marchers in Madrid and 55,000 in Barcelona according to the authorities, and many more according to the organisers, Euronews reports. Rents soared by 87% between 2015 and 2025 while wages rose by about 30%, according to El País, cited by Time, and the average rent swallows almost the entire average salary of 16- to 29-year-olds, according to Spain’s Youth Council. Police made at least 75 arrests, the leader of the People’s Party, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, denounced a strike aimed at the opposition, and polls make the right favourite to win the snap election that the prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has called for 29 November.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In South Sudan, Amnesty accuses the UN and Juba of ignoring warnings before a massacre
items.content_html:
The rights group says the authorities and UN peacekeepers knew an attack was being prepared on Abiemnom, where at least 213 people were killed on 1 March. The report comes six weeks before the first elections since independence.

In a report published this week, Amnesty International says South Sudan’s government and the United Nations Mission in South Sudan had enough information and time to prevent the attack of 1 March on Abiemnom, near the Sudanese border, which killed at least 213 people according to the authorities. According to the group, which interviewed 82 people, between 1,000 and 1,500 gunmen from neighbouring Mayom county shot residents, destroyed more than 230 buildings and looted part of the hospital, while the UN mission reinforced its small garrison only once the assault was over. The mission blames resources squeezed by budget cuts, Juba did not respond to Amnesty, which wants an independent inquiry, and the country, whose president, Salva Kiir, dissolved the transitional government in September, is due to vote on 22 December for the first time since independence.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: After seeing Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump’s envoys head to Dublin to meet Volodymyr Zelensky
items.content_html:
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner spent more than two hours at the Kremlin on Thursday, with nothing announced on the substance of the conflict. Moscow says they backed a humanitarian mission to Kostiantynivka.

On Thursday 12 November Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin, received America’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, at the Kremlin for more than two hours, a day after two days of three-way talks in Abu Dhabi ended in a prisoner-exchange deal, according to TASS and ABC News. The Kremlin’s foreign-policy adviser, Yuri Ushakov, called the meeting “constructive” and said the Americans supported a Russian proposal for a humanitarian mission to Kostiantynivka, in the Donetsk region, and that the three-way talks would continue, but said nothing on territory, which Moscow demands and Kyiv refuses to cede. The two envoys are expected in Dublin on Thursday evening to see Volodymyr Zelensky, who doubts they will bring back “something concrete”, while a Russian drone strike on a block of flats in Kyiv killed a woman and injured seven people that morning, according to Meduza and ABC News.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Israel is reportedly readying a strike on Iran as two supertankers explode in Hormuz
items.content_html:
Israel’s security cabinet has reportedly ordered the army to step up preparations for an attack, according to the public broadcaster Kan. In Hormuz, the Revolutionary Guards say two supertankers were disabled by explosions.

On the evening of Wednesday 11 November Israel’s security cabinet, chaired by the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, ordered the army to step up preparations for an attack on Iran, according to the public broadcaster Kan, cited by Al Jazeera, even as Gadi Eisenkot urged him not to deploy the army without a direct and immediate threat. That same night two supertankers were disabled by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings, the Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday, threatening the same fate for any ship that co-operates with the American armed forces, according to Reuters. Donald Trump says he is ready to return to war if Qatar’s mediation fails, even though his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, thinks the blockade effective enough to make that unnecessary, and Brent closed at $92.76 on Wednesday after Tehran rejected moving its enriched uranium to a third country, according to Al Jazeera.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Ebola in DR Congo passes 11,000 confirmed cases and 5,300 deaths
items.content_html:
Figures published on Tuesday by the Congolese government confirm an outbreak of exceptional scale, the second-largest ever recorded. No vaccine or treatment is approved against the Bundibugyo strain.

According to figures published by the Congolese government on Tuesday 10 November, the Ebola outbreak declared in mid-May in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo now stands at 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths, the worst in the country’s history, Reuters and the AP report. Caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine or treatment has been approved, it has reached eight of the country’s 26 provinces, above all Ituri and North Kivu, where insecurity hampers access to treatment centres and many patients die at home, according to Reuters. It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, after West Africa’s in 2014-2016, and the vaccine trial launched in Bunia at the end of October is not expected to produce results before 2027, while Kenya has recorded nine cases and Nigeria one imported case.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.
tags: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo

items.title: At COP31, António Guterres urges world leaders to be done with fossil fuels
items.content_html:
Addressing the leaders’ summit in Antalya, the UN secretary-general said a temporary overshoot of 1.5°C was now inevitable. He wants an end to new coal, oil and gas projects.

On Wednesday 11 November, addressing the COP31 leaders’ summit in Antalya, Turkey, the UN secretary-general, António Guterres, said that overshooting the 1.5°C warming threshold was “now inevitable” and called for an end to all new coal, oil and gas projects. Global emissions would need to fall by about 6% a year, whereas national plans deliver a third of that at best and point to more than 2.5°C of warming by the end of the century, he said, before proposing a tax on oil companies’ windfall profits. Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, lamented that climate had vanished from G7 and G20 speeches, Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian demanded compensation for the environmental damage done by wars, and the negotiations, led by Australia, are due to end on 20 November.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In northern Tigray, Ethiopia’s army and Eritrean forces are reported to be clashing around Badme
items.content_html:
Having retaken most of Tigray in October, the federal army is pushing towards the Eritrean border. Addis Ababa accuses Asmara of invasion; Asmara calls that a pretext for war.

On Monday 9 November Ethiopia’s federal army and Eritrean forces reportedly clashed around Badme, a long-disputed border town, according to observers cited by the Critical Threats Project, which could not confirm it, after the Ethiopian army took Sheraro and Adi Awala on 3 November. Since late September federal troops, allied with a breakaway Tigrayan faction, have been fighting the forces of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, and Addis Ababa accuses Eritrea of an “invasion” reaching 60km into Tigray, which Asmara portrays as a pretext for a war of aggression. The prime minister, Abiy Ahmed, who regards his country’s access to the Red Sea as inevitable, installed an interim government in Tigray in mid-October, while Chinese envoys were received in Addis Ababa in early November and then by Eritrea’s president, Isaias Afwerki, in an effort to avert open war.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree a vast prisoner exchange in Abu Dhabi, but no breakthrough
items.content_html:
The American-brokered talks ended on Wednesday with an agreement in principle covering more than 1,000 prisoners on each side, according to Moscow. Nothing moved on territory, and America’s envoys are expected at the Kremlin on Thursday.

On Wednesday 11 November, after a second session of under two hours in Abu Dhabi, Russia and Ukraine announced an agreement in principle on a large prisoner exchange, which the Russian general Alexander Zorin says will be the biggest of the war, with more than 1,000 people on each side, according to TASS. Ukraine’s chief negotiator, Rustem Umerov, called the swap the “main result” of the talks, but nothing moved on territory: Russia’s negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, repeated that Moscow would recover “every inch” of the land it claims, while Kyiv still insists on a ceasefire first. The American envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are due to meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday and then Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin, and the exchange, whose numbers are to be settled on Thursday, could take place within two or three weeks, the Russian side told the AP.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: France accuses Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of sabotaging the fridges of 700 shops
items.content_html:
France’s foreign minister blames a cyber unit linked to the Guards for the attack on supermarkets on 12 October. Iran’s ambassador has been summoned and Paris wants European sanctions.

On Monday 9 November France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, blamed Iran’s Revolutionary Guards for the cyber-attack which, on the night of 11-12 October, tampered with refrigeration in some 700 French shops, including Carrefour, Monoprix, Intermarché and Coopérative U stores. According to ANSSI, France’s national cyber-security agency, the attack was the work of Shahid Kaveh, a unit linked to the Guards and betrayed by traces of Persian and Iranian IP addresses, and temperatures rose as high as 50°C for about six hours, the AP reports. Paris has summoned Iran’s ambassador and wants European sanctions, which EU foreign ministers could discuss on 16 November, while Tehran dismisses the accusations as “baseless and biased”.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Indonesia’s vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, resigns amid doubts over his diplomas
items.content_html:
The son of the former president Joko Widodo handed his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto on Wednesday, after court rulings found his school qualifications wanting. Parliament will then have 60 days to elect a successor.

On Wednesday 11 November Indonesia’s vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, handed his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto at a meeting at Halim Perdanakusuma air base in Jakarta, his ally Budi Arie Setiadi, chairman of the Projo organisation, confirmed to Reuters and the Antara news agency. The son of the former president Joko Widodo had been under pressure since the Constitutional Court and then the Supreme Court ruled that his studies abroad did not meet the requirements for his candidacy in 2024, and 120 legislators had just filed a petition demanding his impeachment. According to the senior law minister, Yusril Ihza Mahendra, Parliament must declare the post vacant and then, within 60 days, elect a successor from two names put forward by the president, an uncertainty that is weighing on investor confidence, Reuters notes.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Haiti, Salvadoran troops destroy the house of the 400 Mawozo gang’s leader
items.content_html:
El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, on Tuesday claimed the assault on the gang’s headquarters in Croix-des-Bouquets, where its leader was absent. American diplomats complain that El Salvador is acting without co-ordinating with the UN-backed force.

At around 2.30am on Sunday 8 November a drone unit of the Haitian police, backed by Salvadoran soldiers and helicopters, destroyed the house of Wilson Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, in Croix-des-Bouquets near Port-au-Prince, described as his headquarters. El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, who had vowed to raze the house, claimed the operation on Tuesday; it reportedly left about 20 dead according to the Miami Herald, a toll AFP could not confirm, and Wilson Joseph was absent, according to the Salvadoran press. Haiti’s prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, praised El Salvador, but American diplomats complain that the 2,000 or so Salvadoran soldiers, most of them outside the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, are not co-ordinating with it, according to Axios.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Niger has taken in nearly 64,000 refugees from Nigeria since January, says the UNHCR
items.content_html:
Jihadist and criminal violence in northern Nigeria is driving tens of thousands of people into a drought-stricken neighbour. For lack of money, only 5% of the new arrivals have been registered.

On Tuesday 10 November the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said that nearly 64,000 people had fled northern Nigeria for Niger since the start of the year, and several hundred more for Benin, driven out by Boko Haram, Islamic State West Africa and criminal gangs. Most settle in the border regions of Diffa, which accounts for more than 70% of the security incidents recorded in Niger this year, and Tahoua, where they lack food, water and shelter, while malnutrition and respiratory infections are spreading. The UNHCR is appealing for $11.4m for Niger, Nigeria and Benin, at a time when Niger was already hosting more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers and drought threatens the harvests of some 700 of the region’s 1,000 villages.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Abu Dhabi, Russians, Ukrainians and Americans reopen talks, with Europeans kept in the wings
items.content_html:
Delegations from the three countries meet on Tuesday and Wednesday in the United Arab Emirates, together for the first time since February. The Europeans will be on hand, but Moscow refuses to let them join talks focused on security.

Two days of talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States, represented by the envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, open in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday 10 November, the first three-way meeting since February, when the war with Iran pulled Washington’s attention away. Moscow still demands that Ukraine withdraw from the Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions and give up on NATO, while Kyiv refuses to cede territory Russia has not conquered and wants a ceasefire first, so none of the analysts consulted by Al Jazeera expects a peace deal. A European team led by Björn Seibert, Ursula von der Leyen’s chief of staff, along with French, German and British advisers, will be present, but the Kremlin insists they will not take part in the talks, which Sergei Lavrov says will open with security.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Kraków’s Market Square gunman dies as terrorism investigators look for possible accomplices
items.content_html:
The man behind Saturday’s shooting, which killed six people in the city’s historic heart, died in hospital on Monday. Prosecutors, who are treating it as terrorism, are now cautious about his ideological motives.

At 4.30am on Monday 9 November the 24-year-old Pole who had opened fire from his car on Kraków’s Market Square at around 3pm on Saturday, killing six people and wounding fifteen, died in hospital, the police announced. The dead include four Poles, a Briton and an Austrian woman, and the bodies of the gunman’s father, mother and sister were found at the family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, some 150 kilometres to the north-east. The national prosecutor’s office, which has opened a terrorism investigation, is trying to establish whether others inspired or helped the attacker, as Poland emerges from two days of national mourning and celebrates its independence day on Wednesday.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Nvidia investigates its boss, Jensen Huang, over ties to a woman suspected of spying for Beijing
items.content_html:
The board of the AI-chip giant has handed an inquiry to independent directors after its chief executive’s admission. Three House committee chairmen want to question him behind closed doors.

On Sunday 8 November Nvidia’s board announced an investigation by a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside lawyers, after its chief executive, Jensen Huang, admitted an intimate relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data-centre company. According to the New York Times, American intelligence concluded that she was passing information to Beijing, which China dismisses as baseless speculation, and a Malaysian company linked to Megaspeed bought at least $4.8bn of equipment built on Nvidia technology. The board says it has no reason to believe that national security or confidential information was compromised and retains confidence in its boss, whom three House committee chairmen want to question in a closed-door session on 18 November.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.
tags: Nvidia and the China spying claims

items.title: South Africa’s ANC suffers its worst setback as the big cities hunt for coalitions
items.content_html:
Nelson Mandela’s party won only about 31% of the vote in the local elections of 4 November, ahead of the Democratic Alliance. With no majority, several big cities, including Pretoria and Durban, will have to be run by coalitions.

With 99% of ballots counted in the local elections of 4 November, the African National Congress (ANC) had 30.8% of the vote, down from 45.6% in 2021, and the Democratic Alliance (DA) 24%, according to the chairman of the electoral commission, Mosotho Moepya. The ANC’s secretary-general, Fikile Mbalula, called the result “catastrophic”, while Jacob Zuma’s uMkhonto we Sizwe party, third with nearly 10%, came first in Durban, and the Economic Freedom Fighters slipped to 6.2%. Cape Town gave the DA an outright majority, but Pretoria and Durban remain hung, and the bargaining begins little more than a year before the ANC conference that is due, in December 2027, to choose Cyril Ramaphosa’s successor as party leader.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Yemen, at least 30 killed at a market near Taiz, with each side blaming the other
items.content_html:
The Houthis accuse Saudi aircraft of bombing the Al-Hadara market on Friday; the recognised government blames Houthi missiles. According to the Yemen Data Project, October was the deadliest month for civilians since 2017.

At around 7am on Friday 6 November strikes hit the Al-Hadara market in the Al-Waziyah district of Taiz province, killing at least 30 people and wounding eight, according to the Houthi authorities, a toll the Associated Press could not verify. The Houthis’ military spokesman, Yahya Saree, blames Saudi aircraft, while the spokesman for government forces, Colonel Majed al-Nazili, attributes the carnage to Houthi ballistic missiles and calls it a “war crime”. The attack is part of an escalation that began in July with the collapse of the UN-brokered truce, as the Houthis have besieged the city of Taiz for a month and the government’s “Dawn of Yemen” offensive, launched on 5 October, grinds on.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Gadi Eisenkot accepts the mandate in Israel and calls for a national emergency government
items.content_html:
The former army chief was formally asked on Sunday to form a government, with 67 recommendations but a bloc of only 48 members. He has invited Likud to join him and set four conditions for any partner.

On Sunday 8 November, at the presidential residence in Jerusalem, Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, formally handed Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party, the mandate to form the next government, a day after announcing his choice. Recommended by 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, the former chief of staff commands a bloc of only 48 and has promised creative, unconventional political moves to build a national emergency government. He has until 6 December, extendable to 20 December, to assemble a majority, while the new members are due to be sworn in on Tuesday and Mr Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Houthi attack damages an Aramco tower in the heart of Riyadh’s financial district
items.content_html:
Missiles fired from Yemen were intercepted over the Saudi capital on Sunday, but debris struck a building belonging to the oil giant. The Houthi authorities accuse Saudi aircraft of killing dozens of people near Sanaa.

Overnight on Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November Saudi air defences intercepted Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh, but debris blew out the windows of several floors of an Aramco building in the King Abdullah Financial District, causing no casualties, according to the energy ministry. The Iran-aligned Yemeni rebels have stepped up their fire on the kingdom’s ports and airports since September, and their spokesman, Yahya Saree, claims they also targeted Riyadh’s international airport, which the Saudi authorities have not confirmed. The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed missile launchers in Saada and Sanaa, while the Houthi-run health ministry reports at least 33 people killed on Saturday and 40 on Sunday in Saudi strikes near the Yemeni capital.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: In Ukraine 850,000 people lose power ahead of the talks in Abu Dhabi
items.content_html:
Fresh Russian strikes hit the power grid on Sunday, notably in the Dnipropetrovsk region, and the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost its external power supply. Paris says Europeans will take part in the talks on 10 and 11 November.

Overnight Russian strikes on Sunday 8 November left more than 850,000 people in Ukraine without electricity, over 600,000 of them in the Dnipropetrovsk region, according to the energy company DTEK, while one person was killed and three wounded in Dnipro. The Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost its external power and is running on diesel generators, and a drone hit the site in Komyshuvakha where an earlier strike killed at least 55 people, targeting rescuers, according to Kyiv. France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, announced that France and other Europeans would join the talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November, which had until now been conceived as a meeting between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: COP31 opens in Antalya as the world looks set to overshoot 1.5°C
items.content_html:
Nearly 200 countries meet in Turkey until 20 November for the UN climate conference, presided over by Ankara with Australia leading the negotiations. Current policies point to 2.8°C of warming, according to the UN’s latest projection.

The 31st UN climate conference opens on Monday 9 November in Antalya, Turkey, bringing together delegations from nearly 200 countries until 20 November under the presidency of Turkey’s environment minister, Murat Kurum. Scientists consider it almost certain that warming will exceed 1.5°C in 2026, and current policies point to a rise of 2.8°C by the end of the century, according to the UN’s latest projection, cited by the German news agency DPA. Australia’s climate minister, Chris Bowen, will chair the negotiations, an unprecedented division of roles, ahead of a leaders’ summit on 11 and 12 November at which markedly fewer heads of state are expected than at recent COPs.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Myanmar’s army kills eleven people in an air strike on a school in Sagaing
items.content_html:
Teachers and children were among the victims of a bombing on Saturday in Kani township, according to independent Burmese media. The National Unity Government counted 641 army air strikes in October.

At around 11.30am on Saturday 7 November an air strike by Myanmar’s army hit a school and the village of Nyaung Pin Le, in Kani township in the Sagaing region, killing eleven people, most of them teachers and children, according to independent media. The bombing is part of an air campaign that killed 212 civilians in October, 23 of them children, according to the exiled National Unity Government, nearly six years after the coup and seven months after Min Aung Hlaing was elected president. Fighting continues in Mon State, where more than 15,000 residents have fled Kyaikto township, and in Rakhine, while from 9 November the army is closing checkpoints at night in three Sagaing townships.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Isaac Herzog asks Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, to form Israel’s next government
items.content_html:
On Saturday evening Israel’s president gave the leader of Yashar, backed by 67 members of the Knesset, the job of building a coalition. Benjamin Netanyahu accuses his rival of wanting to govern with “supporters of terrorism”.

On the evening of Saturday 7 November Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, announced that he would ask Gadi Eisenkot, a former chief of staff who leads the Yashar party, to form the next government, with the mandate to be handed over formally on Sunday at the presidential residence in Jerusalem. The former general was recommended by 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members, including the Arab parties, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, but his own bloc holds only 48 seats and several of his allies refuse to depend on Ra’am and the United List. Mr Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14, to muster at least 61 members, while the outgoing prime minister is calling for a “national unity government” that would include his far-right allies and the ultra-Orthodox parties.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Iran lifts the range limit on its missiles after fresh American strikes in Hormuz
items.content_html:
The Revolutionary Guards say they no longer observe a 2,000km ceiling on their ballistic missiles. Washington has set up a force to hunt down Iranian arms smuggling, as advisers urge Donald Trump to resume the war.

On Saturday 7 November the spokesman for the Revolutionary Guards, General Hossein Mohebbi, said in Tehran that the 2,000km limit Iran had imposed on the range of its ballistic missiles had been lifted, a day after American strikes on air defences on Qeshm island. The announcement, which does not say whether Iran already has longer-range missiles, came alongside a statement attributed to the Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, promising a response “without geographical limits” to any American or Israeli threat. According to NBC, advisers have urged Donald Trump to resume large-scale operations before the new Congress sits in January, and America’s Central Command has announced a force to cut the land and Caspian routes by which Iran obtains weapons.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Russia fires 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv three days before talks in Abu Dhabi
items.content_html:
Overnight on 6-7 November Russia targeted the capital’s power grid and damaged the North Bridge over the Dnipro. Volodymyr Zelensky accuses Moscow of preparing for negotiations “by launching ballistic missiles”.

Overnight on Friday 6 and Saturday 7 November Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its region, only four of which were shot down for want of Patriot interceptors, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky, along with 172 drones across 13 regions, wounding at least nine people, including a child. The strikes hit the substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants to the capital, leaving parts of the city without electricity, heating and water, and damaged the North Bridge, which Moscow says it was aiming at. Ukrainian, Russian and American delegations are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday 10 November for a fourth round of talks brokered by Washington, as the death toll from the strike on Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, reaches 55.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Hoax bomb threats spread to European newsrooms after targeting dozens of flights
items.content_html:
Ireland’s public broadcaster, RTÉ, evacuated its offices on Friday after a threatening email, as did Bulgaria’s Nova TV. Nearly 30 flights have been targeted since Tuesday, and no explosives have been found.

On Friday 6 November emails signed by one “Mikhail Andropov” and headed “Message to the West” threatened Ireland’s public broadcaster, RTÉ, which evacuated its offices and suspended programming, as well as Bulgaria’s Nova TV, while Sky reported a threat in Britain. The messages extend a wave of alerts that has disrupted nearly 30 flights in Europe since Tuesday, prompting diversions and fighter-jet escorts, though no explosives have been found, according to Reuters, which could not establish where the emails came from. No country has named a culprit, but Spain’s foreign minister, José Manuel Albares, has denounced a “hybrid aggression”, and NATO has ordered air patrols near the border between Hungary and Romania.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang reaches out to the state as Salvadoran troops close in
items.content_html:
Wilson Joseph’s gang says it has contacted the national disarmament commission and wants UN mediation. The prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, has announced the killing of a gang leader in Cité Soleil.

On Friday 6 November the 400 Mawozo gang, led by Wilson Joseph, told the Associated Press that it had contacted Haiti’s national commission for disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration in the name of “peace” and “national reconciliation”. Accused by the UN and human-rights groups of rape, murder and kidnapping, which it denies, the gang fears an offensive by the more than 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers deployed in recent weeks, and El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, has promised to destroy its leader’s house. The same day the prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, announced the death of a gang leader in Cité Soleil, identified by police as the head of the Boston gang, while the disarmament commission says it is following the government’s road map.

items.title: Paraguay’s Santiago Peña is removed and confined to his home as Pedro Alliana takes over
items.content_html:
The Senate on Friday removed the head of state, brought down by the collapse of Ueno bank, and his vice-president was sworn in at once. Prosecutors have ordered the former president to stay at home in an inquiry into suspected breach of trust and influence-peddling.

On Friday 6 November Paraguay’s Senate removed President Santiago Peña from office, by the unanimous vote of the 44 senators present according to the Associated Press, a day after the lower house impeached him, and Vice-President Pedro Alliana was sworn in in Asunción to serve out a term that runs until August 2028. Prosecutors promptly ordered the former head of state to remain at home, suspecting him of breach of trust, attempted fraud and influence-peddling in the affair of Ueno bank, seized on 3 November, where the public pension fund had placed $355m beyond legal limits. Mr Peña, whose resignation Congress refused and who thereby forfeits the life seat in the Senate promised to former presidents, appeared before prosecutors on Saturday morning; they have also issued an arrest warrant for the former central-bank governor, Carlos Carvallo.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: America strikes Iranian air defences in the Strait of Hormuz as Tehran vows to respond
items.content_html:
Donald Trump confirmed on Friday evening “minor” strikes on an anti-aircraft system on Qeshm island, where Tehran says it shot down an American drone. Iran’s army promises an “immediate” response, while Qatar denies that negotiations have failed.

On Friday 6 November Donald Trump confirmed that American forces had carried out what he called “minor” strikes on an air-defence system on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian state media reported two explosions and where Tehran says it shot down an American drone. The strikes, the first since the Republicans’ defeat in the midterm elections, which the president blames on the war, come as he speaks both of “progress” with Tehran and of possibly destroying “the rest of Iran”, while Qatar, the mediator, denies that negotiations have failed. On Saturday the Iranian army’s spokesman, Mohammad Akraminia, promised an “immediate” response without geographical limits on the supreme leader’s orders, while Tehran still insists that its conditions, including an end to the American blockade and to sanctions, be met before any nuclear talks.

Written by an AI from the sources cited.

items.title: Death toll from the Komyshuvakha strike passes 50 in Ukraine ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi
items.content_html:
Ukraine’s emergency services on Friday raised to at least 50 the death toll from the bombing of an aid centre in the Zaporizhzhia region. On the front line, Russia is barely advancing, according to the Institute for the Study of War.

On Friday 6 November Ukraine’s State Emergency Service raised to at least 50 the death toll from the Russian strike of 2 November on an aid-distribution centre in a former school in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, where dozens of people were still missing. Volodymyr Zelensky describes a double strike with glide bombs, which the UN human-rights monitoring mission says probably violated international law, at the end of a week in which Russia launched 2,346 drones and more than 80 missiles at Ukraine, according to Al Jazeera. On the battlefield Russia has taken only 117 square kilometres in ten months, according to the Institute for the Study of War, while Kyiv has targeted eight Russian refineries in seven days, ahead of three-way talks scheduled for 10 and 11 November in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Avigdor Liberman opens the door to the ultra-Orthodox on the eve of Isaac Herzog’s choice
items.content_html:
The leader of Yisrael Beiteinu says he is ready to govern with the ultra-Orthodox parties but rejects any government reliant on the Arab parties. Israel’s president names the leader tasked with forming a government on Sunday.

On the eve of Sunday’s nomination of the leader tasked with forming a government, Avigdor Liberman, who leads Yisrael Beiteinu, said he was open to a coalition with the ultra-Orthodox parties and to compromises on conscription, while vowing to vote against any government dependent on the Arab parties. Gadi Eisenkot, recommended by 67 of the 120 members of the Knesset against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, owes that lead to the 19 members from Ra’am and the United List, with whom three of the four parties in his bloc refuse to sit, though the bloc has only 48 seats. The Democrats’ leader, Yair Golan, speaks of “progress”, while the Likud lawmaker Miri Regev calls the rival alliance a “bloc of disaster”; the new Knesset will be sworn in on 10 November and will elect a successor to its speaker, Amir Ohana.

items.title: Two new vaccines tested in DR Congo against an Ebola outbreak that has killed over 5,000
items.content_html:
The WHO has added two vaccines designed against the Bundibugyo strain to the trial under way in Ituri. The outbreak, the worst in the country’s history, has more than 10,500 confirmed cases.

On Wednesday 4 November the World Health Organisation announced that two vaccines designed against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, one developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, the other by Moderna, would join the clinical trial under way in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Declared in mid-May, the outbreak, the worst in the country’s history, had more than 10,500 confirmed cases and 5,126 deaths by 1 November, according to WHO figures cited by the UN, and no vaccine or treatment is licensed against this strain, which kills more than half of those infected. The Tumaini trial, launched on 23 October in Bunia, capital of Ituri province, vaccinates the contacts of patients using the so-called ring method, but its results are not expected before early 2027, while the virus has already reached Uganda and Kenya.

items.title: Tankers hit by mines in Hormuz as Iran sets seven conditions for Washington
items.content_html:
Tehran says at least five tankers were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, as the Pentagon stands ready for a resumption of fighting. Through Qatar, Iran has passed a proposal on its nuclear programme to the United States.

On Thursday 5 November Iranian forces reported at least five tankers and a tugboat ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, most of them after striking mines on routes Tehran had not authorised; Britain’s UKMTO agency also reported a vessel hit by two projectiles north of Qatar. The same day, a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran had sent Washington, through Qatar, a proposal on its nuclear programme, to be discussed only once seven demands are met, among them the lifting of sanctions, the unfreezing of Iranian assets and war reparations. The United States, which is studying the text, wants the nuclear issue on the table from the outset, and thousands of American troops stand ready to resume fighting, according to the New York Times, just as several of Donald Trump’s allies distance themselves from the war after the defeat of 3 November.

items.title: Paraguay’s Senate opens Santiago Peña’s impeachment trial after his bid to resign fails
items.content_html:
Congress was unable to accept the president’s resignation on Thursday after his allies walked out, leaving it without a quorum. Senators began his trial on Friday, in his absence, over the collapse of the digital bank Ueno.

On Friday 6 November Paraguay’s Senate opened the impeachment trial of the president, Santiago Peña, who failed to appear, and voted by 39 to 3 to reject his request for another 72 hours to prepare a defence entrusted to the lawyers Ricardo Preda and Adolfo Ferreiro. The day before, his Colorado Party allies had walked out of a joint session of Congress, lacking the votes to accept a resignation that would have earned him a life seat in the Senate with immunity; the charges include his former stake in the holding company of Ueno, the bank seized on 3 November. Removal requires 30 of the 45 senators and would hand power to the vice-president, Pedro Alliana, until August 2028; the defence says it may challenge the process before the Supreme Court and international bodies, while the chief of staff, Javier Giménez, and the interior minister, Enrique Riera, have resigned.

items.title: Ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks, Russian and Ukrainian envoys meet at the White House
items.content_html:
Melania Trump brought together envoys from both countries in Washington on Thursday, with no progress announced. On the ground, Moscow is targeting Ukraine’s energy and logistics networks while Kyiv steps up drone attacks on Russian refineries.

On Thursday 5 November the American first lady, Melania Trump, received Vladimir Putin’s envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, and Russia’s human-rights commissioner at the White House, along with two Ukrainian officials, including the head of the president’s party, David Arakhamia, and urged them to look beyond a mere "temporary ceasefire". The White House credits her with brokering a six-day truce in Oleshky, in the occupied Kherson region, which allowed nearly 800 civilians to be evacuated; the Russian strike of 2 November on an aid distribution in Komyshuvakha, which killed 43 people according to Kyiv, came the day after it expired. The strikes go on: Moscow says it hit a depot of the Nova Poshta delivery company near Kharkiv and a cargo ship off Odesa, while more than 200 Ukrainian drones targeted the Ryazan region, ahead of three-way talks due in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

items.title: Herzog to name Israel’s next prime minister on Sunday, with Gadi Eisenkot in pole position
items.content_html:
With 67 of the 120 members of the Knesset behind him, the former army chief awaits the mandate the president is due to hand out on 8 November. In Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp, down to 46 backers, some cry "stolen" election.

After two days of consultations, Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, called the outcome "clear", with 67 of 120 members recommending Gadi Eisenkot against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, but announced on Thursday 5 November that he would keep talking and would not award the mandate to form a government until Sunday. That tally rests on an unprecedented alliance between the mainly Jewish opposition bloc and the two Arab parties: Ra’am, whose leader, Mansour Abbas, says he wants to enable an "emergency government", and the United List, which would back a minority government from outside. In the outgoing camp positions are hardening: a minister from the far-right Otzma Yehudit party told the head of state that the election had been "stolen", although the electoral commission found no irregularities, and the new Knesset is due to be sworn in on 10 November.

items.title: Somalia’s Supreme Court rules the extension of the president’s term unlawful
items.content_html:
The country’s highest court on Thursday gave the parties thirty days to reach agreement and ninety days to hold elections. The day before, the head of state, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, had sacked the chief justice.

On Thursday 5 November the constitutional chamber of Somalia’s Supreme Court ruled that the constitutional amendments adopted in March could extend neither the term of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, which expired on 15 May, nor that of parliament, and confined the federal government to a caretaker role. The day before, the president had sacked the chief justice, Bashe Yusuf Ahmed, who was hearing an opposition challenge, and replaced him with a close ally, Ibrahim Idle Suleiman; the court declared the dismissal void, and the former prime minister Hassan Ali Khaire accuses the government of sending soldiers into the courthouse. The judges demand an agreement between political parties within thirty days and elections within ninety, whereas the president meant to lead the country to its first direct elections, planned for April and May 2027, a reform whose terms the opposition and several regional parties dispute.

items.title: Midterms: Democrats retake Congress as Trump pays the price for the Iran war
items.content_html:
After a historic election night, the opposition has seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The president admits that the conflict with Tehran weighed heavily on the vote.

On Tuesday 3 November American voters handed the Republicans one of the clearest midterm defeats in recent history: the Democrats won the House of Representatives and took seven Senate seats from them, reaching as far as Texas, which had not elected a Democratic senator since 1988. Donald Trump himself concedes that the war against Iran, launched in February and increasingly unpopular, was a major factor in the defeat, a view shared by his vice-president, JD Vance. Without a majority on Capitol Hill for the last two years of his term, the president will have to deal with an opposition that controls the budget and the power to investigate, while his defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, already faces an impeachment resolution filed by a Republican lawmaker.

items.title: Washington and Tehran: fears of a return to war after the US vote
items.content_html:
Qatar is trying to secure an interim deal before the United States resumes its strikes. Eight months into the conflict, the Strait of Hormuz remains almost closed and oil is above $100 a barrel.

After three days of talks in Doha, the Iranian delegation returned to Tehran without a deal, and messages between the two capitals now pass only through the Qatari mediator. The two sides remain far apart: Washington wants commitments on Iran’s nuclear programme before making any concession, while Tehran makes reopening the Strait of Hormuz conditional on lifting oil sanctions, unfreezing its assets abroad and ending the fighting in Lebanon. American strikes have never fully stopped: the island of Qeshm was hit again on 2 November, and Donald Trump, who had promised not to launch a new offensive before the elections, has not ruled out further operations.

items.title: Russia strikes civilians and the power grid in Ukraine ahead of new talks
items.content_html:
A Russian strike on a school where humanitarian aid was being handed out has killed at least 43 people in the Zaporizhzhia region, as Moscow keeps pounding the power grid. Ukrainian, Russian and American delegations are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

On Monday 2 November, nine Russian aerial bombs hit an underground school in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, while humanitarian aid was being distributed; by Thursday the death toll had reached 43, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky, and dozens more people may still be trapped under the rubble. Meanwhile, drones and missiles are hitting power stations and substations in nine regions, a campaign which, according to the Institute for the Study of War, an American think-tank, aims to make each winter more painful for civilians in order to force Ukraine to give ground. It is against this backdrop that the three delegations will meet in Abu Dhabi to discuss post-war security guarantees, de-escalation and humanitarian measures, after three fruitless rounds of talks earlier this year.

items.title: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot wins the backing of most MPs against Benjamin Netanyahu
items.content_html:
Abandoned by the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party, Benjamin Netanyahu gathers only 46 recommendations, against 67 for his rival, who is backed by the Arab parties. In Gaza, a year after the ceasefire, Israeli strikes still claim lives almost every day.

At the end of consultations held by the president, Isaac Herzog, on 4 and 5 November, 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members recommended Gadi Eisenkot to form a government: the opposition’s 48, joined by the two Arab parties, Raam and the Joint List, with 19 seats between them. Benjamin Netanyahu, whose camp won 53 seats on 27 October, now musters only 46, after the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism declined to recommend anyone without guarantees on military-service exemptions for yeshiva students. The head of state is expected within days to ask Mr Eisenkot, who says he wants to form a “Zionist government”, to build a coalition within 28 days, extendable by 14, with the Joint List pledging to back him from outside government.

items.title: In Sudan, a drone war is strangling civilians
items.content_html:
More than three years into the conflict, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces are stepping up strikes on infrastructure. The crisis is now spilling over into neighbouring Ethiopia.

The Rapid Support Forces (RSF), at war with the regular army since April 2023, seized the Sali military base in Blue Nile state on 3 November and are using drones against power stations and depots, leaving hundreds of aid lorries stranded for lack of fuel. A year after the fall of El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur, Amnesty International is still documenting executions, detentions and torture there, and describes a city emptied of the vast majority of its inhabitants. The Sudanese authorities accuse Ethiopia of hosting RSF drone launch sites; Addis Ababa hit back on 4 November by expelling six Sudanese diplomats, raising fears that the conflict could spread across the Horn of Africa.
